name: The MacWilliams identity
about: for a linear code `C` over a finite field with `q` elements, `#C · W_{C⊥}(X, Y) = W_C(X + (q - 1)Y, X - Y)` in `ℤ[X, Y]`, proved from a Poisson summation formula over the code; the Krawtchouk, normalized and self-dual forms follow.

name: Type II lengths are divisible by eight
about: a doubly even, Euclidean self-dual binary code has length `≡ 0 (mod 8)`, by evaluating the MacWilliams symmetry at `(1, i)` against the fourth-root-of-unity symmetry of a doubly even enumerator.

name: The extended binary Golay code
about: the row space of `[I₁₂ | B]`, with the bordered reverse-circulant block of Huffman-Pless, is a doubly even self-dual `[24, 12, 8]` code with enumerator `X^24 + 759 X^16 Y^8 + 2576 X^12 Y^12 + 759 X^8 Y^16 + Y^24`, and deleting any coordinate leaves a `[23, 12, 7]` code.

name: Type II codes over `ℤ/2^r`
about: for `r ≥ 1`, a self-orthogonal code over `ℤ/2^r` has an even unimodular Construction A lattice exactly when it is self-dual with all Euclidean weights divisible by `2^(r+1)`; at `r = 1` this is the binary Type II statement.

name: The discriminant module of Construction A is `C⊥/C`
about: for a self-orthogonal additive code over `ℤ/m`, the discriminant bilinear module of `P_m(C)` is isometric to the actual quotient `C⊥/C`, obtained from the general gluing theorem, with a quadratic version for even `m` and quadratically isotropic `C`.

name: The weight enumerator
about: `W_C(X, Y) = ∑_w A_w(C) X^(n-w) Y^w` with integer coefficients, defined for any set of words, so MacWilliams, the named-code enumerators and the Type II symmetries all concern one polynomial.

name: The Construction A lattice
about: integer vectors of `ℚ^ι` reducing into an additive code over `ℤ/m`, with the dot product divided by `m`, bundled only under self-orthogonality; every dual carrier lives in the same rational space, so `P_m(C)^∨ = P_m(C^⊥)` is a literal equality.

name: Codes as discriminant subgroups
about: reduction modulo `m` identifies the discriminant module of `mℤ^ι` with `(ℤ/m)^ι`, so an additive code pulls back to a subgroup of an actual discriminant group, where the integral-lattices gluing API applies.

name: The Riemann–Roch theorem
about: for `W` the divisor of a nonzero Weil differential, `ℓ(D) − ℓ(W − D) = deg D + 1 − g` for every divisor `D`, over any exact constant field.

name: The Hurwitz genus formula
about: `[k' : k] · (2g' − 2) = [F' : F] · (2g − 2) + [k' : k] · deg Diff(F'/F)` for `F'/F` finite separable with exact constants and `k'/k` finite separable.

name: The divisor of `dx`
about: for a separating element `x` of a field with exact constants, the Weil differential `dx` has divisor `−2 (x)_∞ + Diff(F/k(x))`, which is therefore canonical.

name: The Weierstrass equation of a genus-one field
about: at each rational place `P` of a genus-one field with exact constants, some `x` and `y` with pole divisors `2P` and `3P` satisfy a Weierstrass equation over `k` and generate the field, in the form `y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆` away from characteristic two.

name: Rigidity of automorphisms
about: over an exact constant field, an automorphism of `F/k` fixing `2g + 3` distinct rational places is the identity.

name: Excision

name: The Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms
about: relative singular homology is a homology pretheory satisfying the exactness, homotopy, dimension and, when coproducts are exact in the coefficients, additivity axioms; its exactness, dimension and additivity classes are local copies from mathlib4#38369, awaiting a Mathlib pin.

name: The suspension isomorphism for spheres
about: for the unit sphere `S` of a real inner product space and `p ∈ S`, `H̃ₖ₊₁(S) ≅ H̃ₖ(S ∩ p⊥)`, through the reduced Mayer–Vietoris map of the cover by the complements of `p` and `−p`; without the induction down to `S⁰`, `Hₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ R` is not yet stated.

name: The sporadic presentation table

name: Euler–Poincaré theorem

name: Horseshoe lemma
about: in any exact category, resolutions of a conflation's outer terms, the right one projective, combine to resolve its middle term; with Schanuel's lemma this lifts finite projective resolutions along conflations.

name: Ext-Euler pairing

name: The Hodge decomposition

name: Semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures

name: Deligne's theorem on the bigrading

name: Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures

name: The Hodge numbers partition the dimension
